profile.name: Mayank Vekariya
profile.summary: Electrical engineer and project manager with 4+ years of hands-on renewable and industrial project experience. I bring structure to site execution, from schedules and contractor coordination to technical documentation and commissioning handovers.
profile.availability: Open to renewable energy site and project execution roles.

experience.description: Built a structured SharePoint knowledge hub for 15+ global partners, prepared technical and market reports, and coordinated input from product, sales, and distributor teams.
Analysed 5,000+ research records, co-authored 2 papers, and improved documentation workflows so new contributors could understand methods and responsibilities quickly.
Managed 6 solar PV and motor-engineering projects from delivery and site setup through installation, testing, commissioning, reporting, budget control, HSE follow-up, and client handover.
Maintained Gantt schedules, cost trackers, risk logs, and dashboards while rotating through production, quality, and engineering teams.

projects.title: 5 MW Solar PV Plant Execution
projects.description: Coordinated civil, electrical, and installation activity across a utility-scale solar site with daily progress tracking, issue follow-up, and safety-aware work sequencing.

projects.title: 500 kW Rooftop Solar Installation
projects.description: Managed execution coordination where access, weather, working-at-height safety, toolbox discipline, and installation sequence had to be controlled tightly.

projects.title: Solar Farm Tracker Deployment
projects.description: Supported field coordination across parallel work zones, with attention to alignment checks, sequencing, and rework reduction.

projects.title: Solar-Powered Water Pump Deployment
projects.description: Supported configuration and deployment planning for off-grid solar pumping systems, balancing reliability, cost, and remote-site constraints.

projects.title: Solar Canal Infrastructure Review
projects.description: Analysed canal-top solar as a dual-use infrastructure concept: PV generation above canals can reduce land use, limit evaporation, improve panel cooling, and create new maintenance and structure-cost challenges.
